subject: Capacity uplift & billing payor swap — documentation and PO needed
messages:

Cc: Oliver Bauer <oliver.bauer@aurorasoft.com> , Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity uplift & billing payor swap — initial info

Hi Marcus,

Following up from last week's call — AuroraSoft has approved the +200K token capacity uplift tied to our Q3 rollout. Legal sign-off is pending a short amendment, but Finance asked if we can switch invoicing from the US parent (AuroraSoft, Inc., EIN: 12-3456789) to our EU subsidiary (AuroraSoft GmbH) for any invoices after 1-Apr-2026.

Finance (cc'd: Oliver) will supply a PO. They also requested confirmation of what evidence Redwood needs to treat AuroraSoft GmbH as the invoicing/payor entity (we think VAT certificate and registered company details).

Can you confirm next steps, whether Net30 stays or moves to Net60 for the new capacity, and if there are any additional compliance docs Redwood needs for EU billing?

Thanks,
Marta Schultz
Director, Cloud Partnerships
AuroraSoft Inc.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift & billing payor swap — initial info

Hi Marta — great news on the uplift. Quick answers below and next steps: 

- Docs we need: VAT registration certificate for AuroraSoft GmbH (PDF), company registration (handy but optional), and the PO referencing Redwood deal ID DL-2026-117. For our billing system we also need the billing contact (name/email) for the EU entity.
- Net terms: internally we can keep the existing Net30 for the current contract. For the expanded capacity we can offer Net60 if AuroraSoft's Finance needs 60 days — that will require approval from Revenue Ops. Please say whether AuroraSoft would prefer Net60 for all upcoming invoices or only for the first uplift invoice.
- PO & amendment: If you can share the PO, we'll prepare a short one-paragraph term amendment (no price changes) and route it via DocuSign.

I'll loop in Monica and Karthik to handle the PO intake and revenue ops approval. Monica — can you confirm the Prod Billing workflow to swap payor entity and what evidence fields Billing Ops will require? Karthik — can you run the Net60 ask by RevOps and let us know if there's any policy constraint?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales — Capacity & Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity uplift & billing payor swap — PO received

Thanks for the PO and VAT cert, Oliver — received and uploaded to the deal page. 

Quick update on Redwood's side (operational steps):
- Billing Ops needs the VAT certificate (received), the legal company name exactly as it should appear on invoices ("AuroraSoft GmbH"), and the billing contact email (lena.hoffmann@aurorasoft.com).
- We'll create a new Payor record in the billing system and set the payor effective date to 2026-04-01. Invoices issued on or after that date will show AuroraSoft GmbH as the payor.
- Net terms: I've started a RevOps ticket to approve Net60 for DL-2026-117 uplift invoices only. If approved, the change will be backdated to apply to invoices created after the effective date. Expect a final answer by EOD 3/12.
- Amendment: Marcus, I'll draft the one-paragraph amendment and include a DocuSign link. I'll circulate for signatures once RevOps confirms Net60.

On a practical note: please confirm whether AuroraSoft prefers monthly invoicing for the uplift capacity or a single pro-rated upfront invoice; that'll change how we set up the invoice schedule.

Monica Patel
Senior Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
